style_anatomy_first.overall_style: Flat 2D digital cartoon character-sheet style that puts a bare stick-figure head and limbs on a fully costumed, solid-filled body. Every figure has a large, perfectly round, pure-white head with a bold, even black outline. The face is minimal: two small solid-black vertical-oval dot eyes and one thin line mouth. Brows are short strokes added only when an emotion needs them, and there is no hair, nose or ears. Arms are single thick black lines with sharp angular elbow bends, ending in white oval mitten hands with no fingers. The torso is not a stick. It is a solid clothing silhouette about as wide as the head, sitting on short trouser legs and rounded soft shoes, which makes a stocky figure about 3.7 heads tall. In walking, running and lunging poses the legs become single black stick lines that still end in the cuffed shoes. Clothing and props use flat, muted, desaturated earth tones (taupe, olive-grey, khaki, camel) with bold black outlines, jagged torn hems, and a few small clusters of dark-brown tick marks for texture. There are no gradients and no cast shadows, and everything floats on a pure white background. Overall it reads as a clean, lightly hand-inked explainer illustration: comic-simple faces with believable, practical costumes and tools.
style_anatomy_first.head: A perfect geometric circle that never squashes, stretches or changes shape in any view or pose. Fill is pure white (#FEFEFE, the same as the paper). The outline is solid black and even, about 4.4% of the head diameter (4 px on a 90 px head). The head diameter is about 27% of standing height (90 px of a 332 px figure in the turnaround) and about the same as shoulder width. There is no hair, no scalp line, no ears, no nose bump and no jaw or chin; the profile and back views are the same plain circle. The head sits directly on the collar with almost no neck. Turning, tilting or looking down is shown only by sliding the facial marks around inside the circle. It is the largest, brightest single shape on the figure.
style_anatomy_first.face:
Front view: two solid black vertical-oval eye dots, about 7-8% of head diameter (D) wide and 10-11% D tall (about 6-8 x 10 px). They are level, about 35-36% D apart centre to centre, and sit at the head's vertical centre (50% from the top on the body heads, about 46% on the expression heads). The mouth is a single thin stroke about 3% D thick and 35-45% D wide, centred at about 67-72% of head height. The neutral body face uses a very slight upward curve. Features sit as a small cluster in the middle to lower part of the circle, with lots of empty white forehead above. No nose, cheeks, blush, eyelashes, pupils, highlights or teeth (except the open grins).

3/4 view: the whole eye-and-mouth group slides about 15-20% D toward the facing side and slightly down. Eye spacing compresses about 15% (27 px instead of 31.5 px), and the far eye sits close to the outline.

Profile: one eye dot about two-thirds of the radius from the centre toward the facing edge, at mid-height. The mouth is a tiny upward hook stroke at about 70% height that runs into the outline. No nose.

Back: completely blank circle.

Looking down (sitting and working): eyes drop to about 60-65% height and the mouth sits just above the bottom outline.
style_anatomy_first.eyebrows:
Absent in neutral, smiling and happy faces and in most calm body poses: Front View, side views, Sitting, Stretching, Walking and Holding up. When used, brows are short separate strokes about 20-25% D long, about one eye-height above the eyes. They are as thick as or slightly thicker than the mouth line and have rounded ends. Their shape alone carries the emotion:
- Angry: straight bars slanting steeply down toward the centre (\ /).
- Inspecting Quality (focused or critical): gentler inward-down slant, slightly curved.
- Sad: curved arcs with inner ends raised and outer ends drooping.
- Worried: wavy tilde strokes with raised inner ends.
- Scared and Surprised: small round arches lifted high on the forehead.
- Confused: asymmetric, one low and flat, one high and arched.
- Determined: flat horizontal bars pressed right onto the tops of the eyes.
- Laughing: thin raised arcs.
- 3/4 Front View: thin arched brows even in a neutral expression (inconsistent with the Front View).
style_anatomy_first.neck_torso:
Neck: essentially none. The bottom of the head touches the collar. In front views a small white V of skin (paper white) shows inside the V-neck between the apron straps. In profile there is only a few-pixel sliver with one short vertical line. In the back view the head sits straight on the tunic.

Torso: a solid costume block, not a stick and with no body line visible under the clothes.
- Shoulders: about 0.95-1.0 D wide, gently sloped, with frayed cap-like flaps of the sleeveless tunic sticking out past where the arms start.
- Chest: about 0.75-0.8 D wide.
- Hem: a slight A-line flare back to about 1.0 D.
- Length: head bottom to tunic hem is about 1.9 D (about 51% of total height). The tunic reaches mid-thigh or knee.
- Arm sockets: in side and 3/4 views, a darker outlined oval "armhole" patch on the shoulder (#6E6758) is where the stick arm comes out.
Posture is upright and relaxed, with a slight forward lean in action poses (about 15-30 degrees when running or lunging).
style_anatomy_first.arms_hands:
Arms: single solid black lines, heavier than the outlines, about 6-7% D (about 1.5x the head outline). They have round caps and come out from under the shoulder flap or armhole patch. Shoulder to wrist is about 1.1 D; upper arm and forearm are roughly equal. Hanging arms form a narrow A, about 10 degrees out from vertical with a very gentle outward bow, leaving a clear white gap of about 0.15 D beside the torso. The hands then reach mid-thigh, about 0.25 D above the tunic hem. Bent arms make a crisp angular V at the elbow, with no rounded joint and no thickening. In side views the near arm is drawn on top of the torso, straight down.

Hands: white (#FEFEFE) vertical egg-shaped ovals, about 0.19 D wide x 0.31 D tall, with a black outline the same weight as the head outline. The arm line joins at the top centre. There are no fingers, at most a barely visible thumb notch on the inner side. When gripping, the oval is drawn on top of the prop at the grip point: the middle of a bone shaft, the top corner of a hide, the shoulders of a garment, or a pole. The same oval clamps over an edge, sometimes turned horizontal.
style_anatomy_first.legs_feet:
Static poses (standing, inspecting, holding up, sitting):
- Legs: two separate trouser tubes in dark taupe (#766B56) with black outlines. Each is about 0.33 D wide with a gap of about 0.18 D. The visible length from tunic hem to sole is only about 0.75-0.8 D (about 21% of height). They carry small pairs of short dark crease dashes.
- Ankle wraps: about 0.13 D tall, drawn as two rolled bands with a pale seam line between.
- Shoes: rounded soft moccasin-boots (#74654F), about 0.34 D long x 0.22 D tall with flat soles. In front view the toes turn slightly outward; in profile they point the way the figure faces.
- Sitting: the legs cross in front as trouser tubes with the shoes visible.

Dynamic poses (Stretching Hide, Running, Walking):
- The trousers disappear. Each leg is a single black stick line, the same weight as the arms, coming out from under the tunic hem.
- Knees bend with crisp angles: running has a rear leg kicked up behind and a front leg reaching forward; stretching has a long straight rear leg and a bent front leg.
- The legs still end in the same cuffed boots.
- There is never a ground line or floor shadow.
style_anatomy_first.proportions:
All measurements are from the 1644x910 source; D = head diameter.
- Overall height: about 3.7 D (turnaround: 332 px tall with a 90 px head; Inspecting Quality: 268 px with a 73 px head). The head is about 27% of height.
- Vertical split: head 1 D; head bottom to tunic hem about 1.9 D; hem to sole about 0.8 D, so the legs are very short and stubby.
- Widths: shoulders about 1.0 D, chest about 0.75-0.8 D, hem about 1.0 D. Each trouser leg is about 0.33 D. Shoes are about 0.34 x 0.22 D.
- Arm: shoulder to wrist about 1.1 D, about 1.4 D including the hand. Hand oval about 0.19 x 0.31 D.
- Line weights: head outline about 4.4% D (4 px). Garment and prop outlines about the same. Limb lines about 6-7% D, about 1.5x the outline. Mouth and brow strokes about 3% D. Interior texture lines about 2% D.
- Eyes: about 0.07-0.08 x 0.10-0.11 D, spaced about 0.35 D apart. Mouth width 0.35-0.5 D.
- Scale across the sheet: action-pose figures are about 0.8x the turnaround scale (heads 68-74 px against 88-90 px). Expression heads are about 1.17x (105 px).
style_anatomy_first.costume_rendering:
Each garment piece is one flat fill with a bold black outline, layered so the parts read by value: light apron over a mid-tone tunic over dark legs and shoes. The reference costume, generalised:
- Tunic: sleeveless, knee-length, hide or coarse cloth in warm grey-olive taupe (#908268). It has a V-neck, frayed cap flaps at the shoulders and a ragged, scalloped, torn hem.
- Bib apron: lighter (#BBAF92). A rectangular bib with a straight top edge sits just under the V-neck. Narrow straps run up beside the neck. The skirt ends a little above the tunic hem with its own torn bottom edge.
- Waist cord / apron tie: pale grey-beige (#CAC4BA), two outlines with a pale fill. At the centre back it has a round knot and two short dangling tails.
- Pouch: rounded leather (#7C6954) with a flap outline, a stitch line and a short pale highlight streak, hung from the cord on the character's right hip. In walking it holds a bone poking out.
- Legs and feet: dark taupe trousers (#766B56), rolled ankle wraps, rounded soft boots (#74654F).
Material and wear are suggested only with line marks:
- deliberately wobbly, irregular contours
- jagged tears and frayed tufts along hems and shoulder edges
- sparse groups of 2-3 short parallel dark olive-brown ticks (#61543B), like hide grain
- a single vertical seam line down the centre back
- 1-3 thin crease strokes for folds, such as diagonal creases on the apron skirt and paired dashes on the trousers
- stitched seams drawn as short dark dashes
There are no patterns, prints, logos, metal, jewellery or saturated colours. Costume fit is boxy and simple, with no anatomy showing through.
style_anatomy_first.props_rendering:
Props use the same bold black outline weight as the figure, flat muted earth-tone fills, simple readable silhouettes and only a few interior strokes. They are realistically scaled to the 3.7-head figure. Wherever a prop is gripped, the white oval hand is drawn on top of it.

Specific props on the sheet:
- Cartoon bone tools: a straight shaft with double-lobed knobs at both ends, ivory (#EBE4D4). One is held across the chest, one is swung in hand, one sticks out of the pouch.
- Bone needle: a thin pale shaft.
- Thread: a long thin pale line with a dark outline, trailing out in a loose curve.
- Raw animal hides: irregular splayed pelt silhouettes with lobes like legs, warm camel (#B39A7D), almost flat with one or two faint fold strokes.
- Hide being sewn: carries a seam of short dark stitch dashes.
- Stack of folded hides (running): 3-4 stacked folded layers, each edge outlined, with darker tan inner folds (#8A7D67).
- Draped hide bundle (walking): hung over the far hip.
- Stretching frame: two straight leaning poles in grey-taupe wood (#828079) with forked Y tips and tight 2-3-ring rope lashings. The pelt is laced to the poles with thin black cords running from its points, plus thin cross-cords along the top and bottom.
- Finished garments: a T-shaped short-sleeve tunic with a V-slit neck (darker inside back of the neckline) and a ragged hem, and a held-up cloth piece, both in tan (#AF997C).
Small effect marks: 3-4 short radiating tension ticks where a hand pulls the hide. No other motion lines, sound effects or speed lines.
style_anatomy_first.line_work:
One bold, constant-width outline around everything, with no tapering, brush calligraphy, sketchy double strokes or hatching.
- Main contours: pure black (#000000-#0F0F0F) for the head, hands, tunic and props. The apron and pouch outlines are a very dark warm brown-black (#140C06).
- Weight: head outline about 4.4% of head diameter (4 px on a 90 px head). Garment and prop contours are similar at about 4 px.
- Limb lines (stick arms and stick legs): the heaviest strokes at about 6-7% D, roughly 1.5x the outline, with round caps and crisp angular bends at elbows and knees.
- Face: eyes are solid black fills. Mouth and brow strokes are about 3% D with round ends; angry and determined brows are a bit thicker.
- Interior details (creases, seams, texture ticks, stitch dashes, fold lines): about 2% D, in dark olive-brown (#61543B) rather than black.
Geometric parts (the circle head and oval hands) are perfectly smooth and vector-clean. Organic parts (garment silhouettes, hems, hides) are lightly wobbly and hand-inked, with jagged, scalloped, torn edges. All strokes are anti-aliased, clean digital ink, comic or webcomic in feel.
style_anatomy_first.shading_and_texture:
Flat colour only:
- no gradients
- no cel-shading shadow shapes
- no highlights or rim light
- no ambient occlusion
- no cast or contact shadows
- no implied light direction
Texture comes entirely from small drawn marks:
- sparse clusters of 2-3 short dark ticks on hide and cloth (more on the rough tunic, fewer on the apron)
- frayed tufts and torn scallops along edges
- a few thin crease and seam lines
- stitch dashes
- a very faint, low-contrast mottled grain inside the garment fills, only a few percent of value variation (possibly compression noise)
Darker flat patches appear only for inner or under surfaces: the shoulder armhole patch (#6E6758) and the inside back of a neckline. The head, the neck V and the hands are pure white and are never shaded or tinted.

style_anatomy_first.background: Pure flat white (#FEFEFE) across the whole sheet, the same white used inside the heads and hands. There is no ground line, no floor or contact shadow, no scenery, no paper texture, no vignette, no panel boxes, frames or dividers, and no tinted bands. Figures float on white, with their feet resting on an invisible common baseline for each row. The only non-white edge element is an 11 px solid black vertical strip down the far left edge, a screenshot or cropping artifact that is not part of the design.
style_anatomy_first.sheet_layout:
The canvas is landscape, 1644x910 px (about 1.81:1, close to 16:9), white, with no borders. It is three stacked horizontal bands. Section labels are left-aligned and every item has a centred caption directly below it. The sheet has exactly 24 illustrated panels (6 + 6 + 12) plus the title block and 2 section labels.

Band 1, turnaround (y about 40-402, about 40% of height):
- Column 0 holds the title block (x about 35-310, y about 45-172): a 2-line bold all-caps title, then a smaller all-caps subtitle line and a lowercase tagline, both indented about 35 px. The white space below it is empty.
- Columns 1-6 hold six full-body views at the same scale. Heads are 88-90 px, head tops aligned at y about 40, soles on a shared baseline at y about 371.
- Figure head centres are at x about 396, 607, 819, 1031, 1254 and 1492. The pitch is about 212 px, widening to about 222-238 px for the two prop or 3/4 views.
- Captions are centred at x about 394, 602, 831, 1034, 1252 and 1496, at y about 384-402.

Band 2, action poses (y about 413-737, about 36%):
- A bold label sits top-left at x about 60-195, y about 417-432.
- Six action poses span the full width at about 0.8x the band 1 scale (heads 68-74 px), feet at y about 655-683.
- Caption centres are at x about 169, 457, 750, 998, 1257 and 1495. Line 1 is at y about 688-712. Captions with a parenthetical continue on line 2 at y about 713-737.

Band 3, expressions (y about 730-893, about 18%):
- A bold label at x about 57-232, y about 730-750, just under the first band 2 caption.
- One row of 12 equal head-only circles, 105 px in diameter, at an exact 130 px pitch: centres x = 113 + 130*i (i = 0..11), y about 812. Gaps are about 25 px and the row spans x about 60-1596.
- A one-word caption sits under each face at y about 873-893.

Margins are about 40 px top, about 35-60 px left, about 48 px right and only about 15 px bottom. Spacing is airy and nothing overlaps.
style_anatomy_first.typography:
All text is a condensed grotesque sans-serif, similar to Roboto Condensed, Helvetica Neue Condensed or Arial Narrow. It is solid near-black (#111111) on white, with no outlines, shadows, colour or decoration. Hierarchy:
1. Title block, top-left: two lines of bold condensed all caps, cap height about 27 px (about 3% of canvas height), tight leading at a line pitch of about 37 px, left-aligned at x about 35.
2. Subtitle line: regular-weight condensed all caps, cap height about 19 px, indented about 35 px.
3. Tagline: regular lowercase, smaller (x-height about 12 px), same indent. Its thin strokes read grey.
4. Section labels "Action Poses" and "Expression Sheet": bold condensed, Title Case, cap height about 16-20 px, left-aligned at x about 55-60.
5. Item captions: regular condensed, Title Case or sentence case, cap height about 19 px (about 2% of canvas height), centred under each item. Long captions break onto 2 lines, with the parenthetical detail on line 2.

Captions read exactly:
- Band 1: "Front View", "Left Side", "Right Side View", "Back View", "3/4 Front View", "3/4 Back View".
- Band 2: "Sitting and Working", "Stretching Hide", "Inspecting Quality", "Running / (and protecting the hide)", "Walking / (carrying tools)", "Holding up finished / finished clothing" (the word is duplicated in the source).
- Band 3: "Neutral", "Smiling", "Happy", "Angry", "Sad", "Worried", "Scared", "Surprised", "Confused", "Determined", "Tired", "Laughing".

The title-block words are third-party branding: "ANCIENT HUMAN / CLOTHING MAKER", "TRUE STICKMAN" and "survival documentary". Never reproduce them; replace them with our own script or character title.

turnaround_views.label: Front View
turnaround_views.description: Square to the viewer, symmetrical, upright and relaxed. Arms hang in a narrow A, about 10 degrees out with a slight bow, and the white oval hands sit at mid-thigh just above the hem. Face: two dot eyes exactly at the head's vertical centre and a soft, very slightly curved smile line about 35% D wide; no brows. The whole costume is visible: V-neck with a white skin V, bib apron with straps, waist cord, pouch on the character's right hip (viewer's left), ragged tunic hem, trouser tubes with a gap, ankle wraps, rounded boots with toes slightly out. Head about 90 px, sole at the baseline.

turnaround_views.label: Left Side
turnaround_views.description: Strict profile facing screen-right. One eye dot about two-thirds of the radius toward the right edge at mid-height, and the mouth a tiny upward hook running into the right edge; no nose. The near arm is drawn over the torso from a dark outlined armhole patch at the shoulder, straight down to a vertical oval hand at hip level. The waist cord knot and two tails hang at the back (left), the pouch shows at the back hip, and the apron is a lighter strip on the front edge. The two legs nearly overlap and the boots point right. The visible flank carries the pouch, so this is anatomically the character's right side.

turnaround_views.label: Right Side View
turnaround_views.description: Mirror of the left profile, facing screen-left. The eye dot and mouth hook are at the left edge. The near arm runs from the armhole patch straight down to an oval hand at hip level. No pouch is visible (this is the character's left side). Cord tails hang at the back (right), the apron strip is on the front (left), the hem is ragged, the legs nearly overlap and the boots point left.

turnaround_views.label: Back View
turnaround_views.description: Completely blank white head circle with no hair or ears. Plain tunic back with one vertical centre seam line and scattered pairs of texture ticks. The pale apron cord crosses the waist with a round knot and two short tails at the centre back. The pouch just peeks out at the character's right hip (viewer's right). Arms hang in a slight A with oval hands at mid-thigh. Jagged hem, trouser tubes with crease dashes, ankle wraps and boots.

turnaround_views.label: 3/4 Front View
turnaround_views.description: Body and face turned about 35-45 degrees toward the viewer's right. The eye dots and mouth slide right and slightly down, and thin arched brows are present. The near (right) arm runs down along the body and bends sharply at the elbow so the hand holds a cartoon bone diagonally across the chest, with the hand drawn over the shaft. The far (left) arm reaches out sideways, bends down and pinches the top edge of a hanging camel-coloured hide at shoulder height. The pouch is on the near hip; trousers, wraps and boots are in a relaxed stance.

turnaround_views.label: 3/4 Back View
turnaround_views.description: Turned away, about 135-150 degrees from the front, facing into the picture toward the upper-left. We see the back plus the left flank, with a blank head circle. The near (left) arm hangs from an outlined dark armhole patch down to an oval hand at hem level, and the far arm hangs along the right edge. The belt knot and tails are slightly right of centre and no pouch is visible. Ragged hem, trouser tubes, ankle wraps and boots.

action_poses.label: Sitting and Working
action_poses.description: Seated cross-legged on the floor (no ground drawn), front or slight 3/4 toward the right. The head looks down, so the eye dots and a short flat calm mouth sit low in the circle; no brows. The right hand is raised at chest height with an angular elbow, holding a white bone needle and drawing a thread. The left hand presses a large camel hide spread over the lap; the hide carries a seam of dark stitch dashes, and a thin pale thread trails off in a curve to the lower right. The crossed legs show as trouser tubes with wraps and boots in front.

action_poses.label: Stretching Hide
action_poses.description: Near-profile facing right in a deep lunge: the rear leg is a long straight diagonal behind and the front leg is bent, both as black stick lines ending in cuffed boots. The torso leans forward about 30 degrees and the pouch hangs at the back hip. Both arms reach forward almost straight: the upper hand grips the top of the near pole and the lower hand pulls the hide edge, with small radiating tension ticks. Face: one eye dot and a small upturned smile hook; no brows. The prop is a leaning frame of two forked-top poles with ring lashings, with a splayed pelt laced to it by thin cords.

action_poses.label: Inspecting Quality
action_poses.description: Standing still, 3/4 facing right, legs in trousers and planted. Both forearms are raised to hold a tan cloth or garment up at face height. The near arm makes a sharp V with the elbow down at chest level and the hand pinching the garment's top-left corner; the other hand clips the top-right corner. Face: brows angled down toward the centre in a focused, critical frown (milder than angry), dot eyes and a short flat mouth, shifted right.

action_poses.label: Running (and protecting the hide)
action_poses.description: Facing right in a full running stride with the torso pitched forward. Both arms wrap a thick stack of 3-4 folded hides against the chest; the near hand shows as an oval under the front of the stack. Legs are black stick lines: the rear leg is kicked up behind with a bent knee and the boot sole up, and the front leg reaches forward and down with a bent knee. The pouch swings at the hip. Face, shifted right: an angry, determined look with steep V brows, dot eyes and a downturned frown.

action_poses.label: Walking (carrying tools)
action_poses.description: Facing right (3/4) in a relaxed mid-stride, legs as black stick lines with the rear boot pushing off and the front boot landing. The near arm swings back with a bent elbow, holding a bone tool pointing back and down, while a second bone pokes up out of the pouch. The far arm carries a bundle of draped hides or garments against the far hip. Face: a gentle content smile with dot eyes, shifted right; no brows.

action_poses.label: Holding up finished finished clothing
action_poses.description: Standing, 3/4 facing left, legs in trousers and planted. Both arms are raised with V-bent elbows, holding a finished short-sleeve T-shaped tunic (V-slit neck, ragged hem) by its shoulders and displaying it to the viewer's left at shoulder height. Face, shifted left: a proud open grin with dot eyes and a D-shaped mouth filled black with a light-grey upper-teeth band; no brows. The pouch appears on the viewer's right hip, which is inconsistent with the other panels.

signature_traits: Head is a large, perfectly round, pure-white circle with a bold even black outline: no hair, ears, nose or skin colour, about 27% of body height, never deformed.
Ultra-minimal face: two small solid-black vertical-oval dot eyes and one thin line mouth set in the middle to lower part of the circle; brows appear only as short strokes when an emotion needs them.
Arms are single thick black stick lines (about 1.5x the outline weight) with crisp angular elbow bends, ending in white, finger-less oval mitten hands outlined in black.
The body is not a stick but a solid flat-filled costume silhouette about as wide as the head, with almost no neck; the head sits straight on the collar.
Stocky, about 3.7-heads-tall build: long tunic-like torso (about 1.9 head diameters) on very short legs (about 0.8 head diameters) with rounded soft boots and rolled ankle wraps.
Static poses use trouser-tube legs; walking, running and lunging switch the legs to single black stick lines that still end in the cuffed boots.
Muted, desaturated earth-tone palette for all clothing and props (taupe, olive-grey, khaki, camel), contrasting with the paper-white head and hands.
Flat fills with no gradients or cast shadows; texture only from sparse clusters of short dark-brown tick marks, thin crease lines, torn or jagged hems and frayed edges.
One bold, constant-width black outline around everything; interior details in thinner dark-brown lines; smooth geometric head and hands against slightly wobbly, hand-inked costume edges.
Turning is shown only by sliding the dot eyes and mouth inside the unchanged circle: shifted in 3/4, a single dot plus a mouth hook at the edge in profile, blank from behind.
Side and 3/4 views show a darker outlined armhole patch on the shoulder where the stick arm comes out; in side views the arm is drawn straight down over the torso.
Plain pure-white background with no ground line or shadows; captioned items laid out in clean rows, captions in a condensed sans-serif.
absent_traits: No hair, scalp line, beard or any head covering on the base character
No nose, ears, cheeks, blush, chin or jaw; the profile stays a perfect circle
No eyelashes, irises, pupils-with-highlights or white eye sclera (except the Tired eyes); eyes are solid black dots
No teeth or tongue, except the light teeth band in one open grin
No skin colour: head, neck V and hands are paper white
No visible neck stick, torso stick or body outline under the clothes
No fingers, nails or detailed hands
No drawn elbow or knee joints and no muscles or anatomy; limbs bend as sharp angles
No gradients, soft shading, cel-shadow shapes, highlights, rim light or ambient occlusion
No cast, contact or ground shadows and no ground line
No background scenery, texture, vignette, panel boxes, frames or dividers
No saturated or bright accent colours, patterns, prints, logos, metal or jewellery
No sketchy pencil lines, cross-hatching, halftone, watercolour or painterly brushwork
No 3D rendering, photoreal textures or realistic proportions
No speech bubbles, sound effects, speed lines or motion blur (only tiny tension ticks)
No sweat drops, blush marks or question or exclamation marks in the expressions
adaptation_notes: Core lock to repeat in every prompt: perfectly round pure-white head with a bold black outline; two small solid-black vertical-oval dot eyes and a thin line mouth; no hair, nose or ears; thick single black-line arms with angular elbows; white finger-less oval hands; solid flat-coloured costume body about as wide as the head; about 3.7 heads tall with short legs and rounded boots; muted earth tones; flat fills with sparse tick-mark texture; bold even black outlines; no gradients or shadows. Give exact proportions (head about 27% of height) and attach the generated reference sheet every time.

Leg rule: the reference mixes trouser-tube legs in static poses with black stick legs in walking, running and lunging poses. To prevent drift, state the rule explicitly in every prompt, or pick one rule for the whole channel. Also fix side-specific accessories in words (for example, 'pouch always on the character's own right hip'), because the source sheet itself slips once.

Modern clothing (The Median Worker): keep the head, face, line arms, oval hands and stocky proportions exactly. Draw the modern outfit with the same method: one flat muted fill per garment, bold black outline, 1-3 crease strokes, sparse ticks only on rough fabrics. Examples: heather-grey hoodie over faded navy jeans; dusty-blue work shirt over khaki slacks; scrubs; delivery vest. Keep the torso block about one head wide and about 1.9 heads to the hip or hem, trousers as short tubes, and shoes as rounded blobs with a sole line. No logos, brand marks or readable text on clothes; keep everything desaturated, with at most one muted accent colour per character.

Distinguishing several characters: never add hair, noses or detailed faces, which breaks the style. Tell characters apart by costume colour from the muted palette, silhouette accessories (headband, shawl, cap, necklace of beads, tool belt, bag, apron), body scale (a child is a smaller body with the same face and a slightly larger head-to-body ratio) and signature props. Give each character a short fixed costume description and repeat it verbatim in every prompt.

Animals: same constant bold black outline and flat muted fills; simple rounded geometric silhouettes; solid black dot eyes identical to the humans'; minimal features (no detailed fur, muscles or realistic shading); fur only as sparse tick marks; limbs as simple filled shapes; realistic size relative to the 3.7-head humans. Show emotion, if needed, only with the same dot-eye and brow vocabulary.

Crowds: reuse the identical character template at smaller scale, keeping outline weight visually bold relative to the figure size. Vary costume tones and accessories rather than faces. Background figures may have dot-eye-only or blank faces. Keep white circle heads readable (space them out, avoid heavy overlaps), drop texture ticks at small sizes, and stand everyone on a consistent baseline or ground plane.

Full 16:9 scenes with backgrounds: draw the environment in the same flat-fill, black-outline vocabulary but quieter, so characters pop. Use thinner outlines (about 60-75% of the character outline), lower contrast and desaturated tints, few texture marks, simplified shapes and a simple ground plane or horizon. Avoid large pure-white areas directly behind the white heads, or give heads a mid-tone backdrop. No photoreal textures, lighting gradients or cast shadows. Keep character height consistent across frames (for example, about 45-60% of frame height for a main full-body beat).

Per-script reference sheet: copy this sheet's structure on pure white with no borders. Band 1: title block plus Front, Left Side, Right Side, Back, 3/4 Front, 3/4 Back for each character, one row per character if there are several. Band 2: every action pose the script uses, each captioned in Title Case with an optional parenthetical second line. Band 3: a row of equal head-only expression circles (the 12 listed or the ones the script needs) with one-word captions in a condensed sans-serif. Use our own title text, never the third-party title, subtitle or tagline.
uncertain: Hex values are estimated from a compressed screenshot; the original flat fills may differ slightly, and the faint mottling inside fills may be compression noise rather than intended texture.

style_costume_first.overall_style: A flat 2D cartoon model-sheet style that puts a minimal stick-figure head and limbs on a fully costumed, earthy body. The head is a large, perfectly round, pure-white circle with a bold, even near-black outline. It has only two tiny solid-black oval dot eyes and one thin mouth stroke, and no hair, ears, nose or drawn neck. The arms are single thick black lines with sharp angular elbows, ending in white outlined oval mitten hands with no fingers. The body wears solid, believable prehistoric work clothes: a ragged sleeveless hide tunic, a lighter leather bib apron, a pale cord belt, a hip pouch, loose leggings with wrapped ankles, and soft rounded moccasins. The clothes are painted in flat, low-saturation taupe, khaki, olive-brown and tan, with warm brown-black hand-inked outlines that wobble slightly, torn zigzag edges, and only a sparse sprinkle of tick-mark texture. There are no shading shapes, gradients, cast shadows, ground lines or backgrounds; everything sits on pure white. The figure is about 3.6 heads tall, and the head is wider than the torso. The style is recognisable from the contrast between the clean, emoji-simple white head and sticks and the gritty, historically grounded, muted costume and props.
style_costume_first.head: Perfect geometric circle, never squashed or foreshortened, the same size and shape in every view. Fill is pure white #FFFFFF, identical to the page; the head is defined only by its outline. The outline is bold, even near-black (#0B0B0B) at about 5% of the head diameter (4-5 px on a 92 px head), smooth and vector-clean with no taper. The head is oversized: about 1.25x the torso width, about 1.0x the shoulder width including the ragged shoulder caps, and about 28% of total figure height. There is no hair, ear, nose, skull bump, jaw or chin; the back and 3/4-back views show a completely blank circle. The bottom of the circle sits directly on the collar. Only in profile and 3/4 does a tiny white neck stub show (about 1/5 head wide, under 1/10 head tall). Turn and tilt are shown only by moving the facial features inside the circle: centred for front view, shifted about 1/4 of the diameter toward the facing side for 3/4, a single eye near the edge for profile, features dropped into the lower third when looking down (seated working pose), and no features from behind.
style_costume_first.face: Eyes: two small solid-black vertical ovals, taller than wide (about 8% x 12% of head diameter, e.g. 7-8 x 10-11 px on a 92 px head). No eye whites, pupils, highlights or lashes. They sit at about 48-50% of head height from the top, about 1/3 of the diameter apart centre to centre, and level. Mouth: one thin black stroke (about 3% of head diameter) at about 67-72% of head height, about 1/3 to 2/5 of the head width. It is straight for neutral and a shallow U for a smile. In profile it is a short line starting at the outline with a tiny upward curl at the inner end. Open mouths are outlined shapes with white interiors: a small vertical O (surprise), a flat-bottomed dome (scared), a big D-shape (laughing), a small horizontal oval (tired). The exception is the proud grin in the "holding up" action pose, which is a black-filled D-shape with a white upper-teeth band. No nose, cheeks, blush, chin line or skin colour. Extra marks appear only with emotion: an outlined white teardrop, laugh-crinkle dashes, under-eye bag lines. On the turnaround the resting face is calm: dot eyes and a faint, nearly straight smile line.
style_costume_first.eyebrows: Absent on calm faces (neutral, smiling, happy, front view, walking smile, stretching profile). They are added only to carry emotion, except for two short, gently arched brows in the 3/4 front view. When present they are short solid-black strokes, about 1/5 of the head width long and 3-4% of the head diameter thick, with rounded or slightly tapered ends, placed just above each dot eye. Vocabulary: straight dashes slanting steeply down toward the centre to form a V (angry, running); slightly curved strokes lowered toward the centre (stern inspecting); curved strokes with raised inner ends (sad); tilde/S-curves with raised inner ends (worried); thin high arches well above the eyes (surprised, scared, laughing); thick flat horizontal bars resting directly on top of the eyes, making a T with each eye (determined); asymmetric, one low wavy dash plus one high arch (confused).
style_costume_first.neck_torso: No neck is drawn in front or back views. The head sits on the collar, and a white V-shaped notch in the tunic neckline reads as neck/chest skin, flanked by the two apron straps. A tiny white neck stub appears only in profile and 3/4. The torso is a slightly tapered upright slab about 0.8 head-diameters wide and about 1 head tall from collar to belt. It is completely covered by clothing; the stick spine is never shown. Vertical landmarks: belt at about 55% of figure height, apron hem at about 74%, tunic hem at about 79% (mid-thigh). Posture is upright and a bit stiff in the turnaround and leans forward 20-30 degrees in action poses. In side, 3/4 and action views a darker, irregular, bean-shaped armhole patch on the tunic shoulder marks where each stick arm comes out.
style_costume_first.arms_hands: Arms are single solid near-black strokes, not outlined tubes, about 6% of head diameter (5-6 px on a 92 px head). That is slightly heavier than the head outline, with round caps. They come out from under the ragged shoulder caps or armhole patches and are drawn over the costume where they cross it, e.g. the profile arm over the torso. At rest they hang in a gentle outward bow a little away from the body, with hands at upper or mid-thigh level (about 71% of figure height; arm length about 1.4 head-diameters). In action they bend at crisp angular elbows made of two straight segments, often a sharp V across the chest. Hands are white ovals with a black outline, slightly taller than wide (about 0.2 x 0.25 of head diameter, e.g. 17 x 23 px), with no fingers, thumb or wrist. When gripping, the oval overlaps or wraps the object (bone, pole, hide edge, garment shoulder), sometimes with one small inner curve suggesting curled fingers. The held object continues on both sides of the hand.
style_costume_first.legs_feet: Clothed legs (turnaround, standing and seated poses): two separate straight columns of loose dark olive-taupe leggings (#746B5A) with slightly wobbly warm brown-black outlines and sparse "=" double-tick marks. A rolled, bulging cuff wraps each ankle, tied off by a thin pale cord (#CAC4BB). Shoes are soft rounded moccasins (#736653) with flat soles and rounded toes, turned slightly outward in front view. Only about 0.75 head of leg shows below the tunic hem. In the dynamic poses (stretching lunge, running, walking) the legs below the hem are drawn as bare single black stick lines, the same weight as the arms, with sharp knee angles, still ending in cuffed moccasins. Stances: front view feet slightly apart, weight even, profile feet staggered; running has the rear foot kicked up near hip height with the knee bent about 90 degrees and the front leg reaching; walking is mid-stride; sitting is cross-legged with knees out and crossed shins in front.
style_costume_first.proportions: Measured on the turnaround: head 92 px, figure 331 px, so about 3.6 heads tall. The head is 28% of height. Action-pose figures are about 0.8x scale (head about 75 px, standing height about 271 px, still about 3.6 heads). Expression heads are about 1.16x the turnaround head (about 107 px). Landmarks as a fraction of figure height from the top of the head: eyes 0.13, mouth 0.20, chin/collar 0.28, belt 0.55, hand tips 0.71, apron hem 0.74, tunic hem 0.79, ankle cuff 0.92, sole 1.00. Widths: head about 1.25x torso; shoulders with caps about 1.0 head; torso about 0.8 head. Line weights relative to head diameter: head outline about 5%, limb sticks about 6%, costume and prop outlines about 4%, facial strokes about 3%, interior detail lines about 1-2%. Hands about 0.2-0.25 head. Eyes about 8% x 12% of head; eye spacing about 1/3 head. Overall a chunky, slightly chibi head on a sturdy, short-legged clothed body.
style_costume_first.costume_rendering: Layered, believable prehistoric work clothing drawn as simple solid flat-colour shapes, each piece with its own outline. (1) Base: loose straight leggings (#746B5A) ending in rolled, bulging ankle cuffs tied with a thin pale cord, over soft rounded moccasins (#736653). (2) Sleeveless hide/fur tunic (#91856D) to mid-thigh. Its rough-cut shoulder caps jut slightly past the arm roots with notched, jagged edges. It has a V-neck, a torn zigzag hem, one vertical seam/fold line down the centre back, sparse fur/hide fleck ticks, and darker bean-shaped armhole patches. (3) Halter bib apron in lighter khaki leather (#B9AE95). The bib has a straight top, two narrow straps rising to the back of the neck, and hangs to just above the tunic hem. Its bottom edge is softly wavy and torn, with 1-3 diagonal fold strokes. It is invisible from behind. (4) A thin pale greige cord belt (#CAC4BB), drawn as a narrow double-outlined band, goes round the waist over the apron. It is wrapped 2-3 times and tied at centre back in a small loop knot with two hanging tails. (5) A rounded leather pouch (#7C6D5B) hangs from the belt on one hip by a loop. It has a curved flap line and 2-3 small grey tool handles poking out of the top. Materials read as hide, leather and cord through muted colour and ragged contours, not detailed texture. Wear shows as torn hems and uneven edges. Fills are flat with plus or minus 3-5% mottling; folds are 1-3 thin dark-brown strokes. No patterns, prints, logos, jewellery, colour accents or metal.
style_costume_first.props_rendering: Props use the same treatment as the costume: warm brown-black slightly wobbly outline (about 4% of head diameter), flat muted fill, sparse dark ticks, simple silhouettes, no shadows. Raw hides and pelts: irregular lobed animal-skin silhouettes with leg flaps and a tail or neck point, flat warm tan #AD9B82 with almost no interior detail. They hang with gravity when held by a corner. Stretched hide: a splayed, star-like shape with about 8 pointed lobes, each tied out by a thin single black cord. Folded hides: stacks of 3-4 offset layers, each outlined, top layers tan and under-layers darker (#8C8473). Finished garment: a T-shaped short-sleeved tan hide tunic with a ragged V-slit neckline (darker inside), ragged hem and short "//" fold ticks at the shoulders. Bone tools: classic cartoon bones (straight shaft, double-knob ends) in ivory #EBE4D5 with a beige #B9AD95 shaded side, plus a slim bone needle. Wooden stretching frame: straight cool weathered-grey poles (#7D7A74) with forked Y tops, lashings drawn as 2-3 parallel wrapped bands, and a crossbar. Thread: a thin double-outlined pale strand ending in a loose curl. A sewn seam is a dashed dark line with small cross-stitches. Interaction cues: white oval hands overlap and wrap props, and short radiating tension ticks appear where a hand pulls a hide. All tools are bone, wood, hide or cord.
style_costume_first.line_work: Clean digital inking with two ink families. (a) The character's stick parts (head circle, facial marks, arm and leg sticks, hand ovals) use neutral near-black #0B0B0B. These lines are smooth, even, round-capped and vector-clean: head outline about 5% of head diameter, limb sticks about 6% (slightly heavier), mouth and brow strokes about 3-4%, eyes solid filled ovals. (b) Costume and props use warm brown-black #15110C at about 4% of head diameter. These contours are slightly wobbly and hand-inked, with jagged, notched or torn edges where the material is hide. Interior lines for folds, seams and ticks are thinner (about 1-2% of head) in dark brown, not black. Every shape is a fully closed outline. No sketchy overdraw, construction lines, hatching or cross-hatching, no line-weight swelling for depth, no heavier outer silhouette stroke. Stick limbs are drawn on top of clothing where they overlap. Anti-aliased digital art with no paper grain.
style_costume_first.shading_and_texture: Essentially flat local colour. Each garment or prop is a single fill with only about plus or minus 3-5% value variation (faint mottling, occasionally a slightly darker band just inside an outline). There are no cel-shadow shapes, gradients, rim light, ambient occlusion or highlights, except the lighter ivory side of the bones. Texture comes from sparse, small, hand-drawn marks in a darker brown of the same hue (about #5A5246): clusters of 2-3 short parallel ticks ("//", "="), about 4-8 per garment panel; tiny specks; one vertical seam/fold line on the tunic back; 1-3 thin diagonal fold strokes on the apron and held leather; dashed stitch lines on sewn hides; short radiating tension ticks where a hand stretches a hide. Ragged contours (zigzag hems, notched shoulder caps, lobed hide outlines) carry most of the weathered leather/fur feel. Head, hands and neck notch are pure flat white with zero shading. The source shows mild compression softness.

style_costume_first.background: Flat pure white #FFFFFF across the whole sheet. No ground line, floor plane or horizon. No cast or contact shadows: the pixels directly under every foot are pure white. No vignette, paper texture, colour fields, panel boxes, borders, frames, dividers or grid lines. Items float in white space and are separated only by spacing. Not part of the design (screenshot/crop artifacts): a black vertical strip about 10 px wide on the far-left edge and a faint grey line along the bottom edge.
style_costume_first.sheet_layout: Landscape canvas 1644x910 px (about 1.81:1, close to 16:9), white, borderless. 24 captioned items in 3 horizontal bands (6 + 6 + 12), plus 1 title block and 2 section headers. Band 1 (y about 4-45%): the title block fills the top-left cell (x about 2-19%, y about 5-19%). To its right, 6 full-body turnaround figures of the same character stand in one row at identical scale (about 331 px tall = 36% of canvas height, head about 92 px). Their head tops are at y about 4.3%, soles on an invisible common baseline at y about 40.7%, and centres at x about 24%, 36.6%, 50.4%, 62.6%, 75.9%, 90.5% (pitch about 210-240 px). Each caption is centred under its figure at y about 42-45%. Band 2 (y about 45-81%): bold header "Action Poses" flush left at x about 3.6%, y about 45.7-47.8%. Then 6 action vignettes in one row at about 0.8x scale (head about 75 px), spanning y about 45-75%, centred at x about 10.3%, 27.9%, 45.6%, 60.6%, 76.5%, 90.9%. Each vignette contains only the figure and its props. Captions are centred beneath at y about 75.8-78.4%; three captions have a second line at y about 78.6-81.4%. Band 3 (y about 80-98%): bold header "Expression Sheet" flush left at x about 3.5%, y about 80-83%, beside the second caption lines of band 2. Then 12 head-only circles (no neck or body) in one evenly spaced row: diameter about 107 px (6.5% of width), pitch 130 px, centres from x about 6.8% to 93.8% in 7.9% steps, vertical centre at y about 89%. One-word captions are centred under each at y about 95.8-98.4%. Margins are tight: about 36-60 px left, about 45 px right, about 4 px top, about 15 px bottom. Dense but uncluttered; no numbering, arrows or rulers.
style_costume_first.typography: All text is a condensed neo-grotesque sans-serif (Roboto Condensed / Helvetica Neue Condensed / Arial Narrow-like); no hand lettering, and no text inside the artwork. Title: bold/heavy condensed, ALL CAPS, 2 lines, black, left-aligned at x about 36 px, cap height about 30 px (about 3.3% of canvas height), line pitch about 39 px, about 273 px wide. Under it are two smaller lines (cap or ascender height about 20 px), regular weight, dark charcoal, indented about 35 px from the title's left edge: the first ALL CAPS (series/brand line), the second all lowercase (genre line). The literal title-block words are third-party branding, recorded only so they can be avoided; never reproduce them: "ANCIENT HUMAN / CLOTHING MAKER", "TRUE STICKMAN", "survival documentary". Section headers "Action Poses" and "Expression Sheet": bold condensed, Title Case, black, cap height about 20 px, flush left. Item captions: regular condensed, dark charcoal (about #252525), cap height about 19 px (about 2.1% of canvas height), centred under each item, Title/sentence case; when a caption is two lines, the parenthetical goes on line 2. Literal captions, row 1: "Front View", "Left Side", "Right Side View", "Back View", "3/4 Front View", "3/4 Back View". Row 2: "Sitting and Working", "Stretching Hide", "Inspecting Quality", "Running / (and protecting the hide)", "Walking / (carrying tools)", "Holding up finished / finished clothing" (word duplicated in source). Row 3: "Neutral", "Smiling", "Happy", "Angry", "Sad", "Worried", "Scared", "Surprised", "Confused", "Determined", "Tired", "Laughing".

turnaround_views.label: Front View
turnaround_views.description: Straight-on and symmetrical, standing at attention. Legs straight and slightly apart, moccasin toes turned slightly outward. Arms hang in a gentle outward bow a little away from the body, white oval hands at upper-thigh level. Face centred: dot eyes at mid-height, faint nearly straight smile line, no brows. Shows the full layering: white V-neck notch between the apron straps, straight-topped bib apron, pale cord belt across the waist, pouch with tool handles on the character's right hip (viewer's left), the apron's wavy torn hem over the tunic's zigzag hem, leggings with rolled ankle cuffs and cord ties.

turnaround_views.label: Left Side
turnaround_views.description: Strict profile facing the viewer's right. One dot eye about 3/4 of the way toward the right edge at mid-height. The mouth is a short line touching the right outline with a tiny upward curl. A tiny white neck stub shows between head and collar. One arm is visible: a straight black stick from a darker bean-shaped armhole patch at the shoulder down to a white oval hand at hip level, drawn over the costume. The apron reads as a lighter front panel. The cord belt is wrapped 2-3 times with a knot and short tails, and the pouch is visible at the hip behind the hand. Torso is a slim upright slab; legs slightly staggered; feet point right.

turnaround_views.label: Right Side View
turnaround_views.description: Mirror profile facing the viewer's left: eye near the left edge, short mouth line touching the left outline. Same darker armhole patch, straight hanging arm and oval hand at hip. The belt knot has a dangling tail at the back (right side of the image). No pouch is visible on this side. The apron panel is on the front edge, legs slightly staggered, feet point left.

turnaround_views.label: Back View
turnaround_views.description: Completely blank white head circle: no hair, ears or features. Plain tunic back with ragged shoulder caps, a single vertical centre seam/fold line and sparse fleck ticks. The pale cord belt is tied at centre back in a small loop knot with two hanging tails. The apron is not visible; a small bulge of the pouch peeks out at one hip. Arms hang symmetrically to hip level. Leggings show '=' ticks, ankle cuffs with pale cord ties, and the heels of the moccasins.

turnaround_views.label: 3/4 Front View
turnaround_views.description: Body and head turned about 45 degrees toward the viewer's right. Facial features are shifted right of centre: two short, gently arched brows, dot eyes, soft smile. The near arm bends at a sharp elbow to hold a cartoon bone diagonally across the waist. The far arm extends sideways at chest height, dangling a raw hide (irregular pelt silhouette) gripped by its top corner. Pouch on the near hip; leggings slightly apart.

turnaround_views.label: 3/4 Back View
turnaround_views.description: Turned about 45 degrees away from the viewer. Blank head; tunic back seen at an angle; darker armhole patch on the near shoulder with that arm hanging along the side. The belt knot and tails sit off-centre, and a lighter sliver of the apron edge shows at the side. Hands at hip level; leggings, ankle cuffs, moccasins.

action_poses.label: Sitting and Working
action_poses.description: Seated cross-legged on the undrawn ground, front view, slightly hunched. The head tilts down, shown by placing the features in the lower third of the circle, with a calm, concentrated face: dot eyes and a short flat mouth. The near hand is raised to chest height holding a slim bone needle that trails thread. The far hand steadies a tan hide garment piece spread over the lap, which shows a dashed stitched seam. A loose thread trails off to the right and ends in a curl. Leggings and crossed moccasins show below the hide.

action_poses.label: Stretching Hide
action_poses.description: Side view facing right in a deep lunge: front knee bent, back leg straight and extended, torso leaning forward about 30 degrees. Both stick arms reach forward. The upper hand grips a frame pole near its forked top; the lower hand presses and pulls the hide's edge, with short radiating tension ticks. The frame is two long cool-grey poles leaning right with Y-forked tops, 2-3-band cord lashings and a crossbar. The splayed tan hide is tied out by about 8 thin black cords. Profile face with one dot eye and a small content smile. Below the hem the legs are bare black stick lines ending in cuffed moccasins.

action_poses.label: Inspecting Quality
action_poses.description: Standing with body and head 3/4 toward the viewer's right. Both hands hold a draped tan leather piece up at face height beside the head, one at each top corner; the near arm crosses the chest in a sharp V. Stern, scrutinising face: slightly curved brows lowered toward the centre, dot eyes, short flat mouth. Legs in leggings, feet planted, pouch at the near hip.

action_poses.label: Running (and protecting the hide)
action_poses.description: Full sprint to the right in 3/4 view, torso leaning forward about 20 degrees. Both arms wrap a stack of 3-4 folded tan hides against the chest: one forearm over the top, white oval hands under the front. Legs are bare black stick lines: the rear leg is kicked up high behind with the knee bent about 90 degrees, and the front leg reaches forward, both ending in cuffed moccasins. Tunic and apron hems flare backward and the pouch swings out at the hip. Angry, determined face: thick brows slanting down to the centre, dot eyes, inverted-U frown. No speed lines.

action_poses.label: Walking (carrying tools)
action_poses.description: Relaxed mid-stride to the right in 3/4 view, upright posture, bare stick legs with cuffed moccasins. The near arm is bent back at a sharp elbow, its hand at hip level holding a cartoon bone horizontally; a second bone sticks up out of the pouch. The far arm carries several folded hides draped over it, hanging at hip level. Pleasant face: dot eyes, soft closed smile, no brows.

action_poses.label: Holding up finished clothing
action_poses.description: Standing with the body 3/4 toward the viewer's left and the head turned toward the garment. Both hands hold up a finished short-sleeved, T-shaped tan hide tunic by its shoulders at chest height, beside the body. The tunic has a ragged V-slit neckline, a ragged hem and short fold ticks. The near arm crosses the chest with a sharp elbow. Proud, delighted face: dot eyes and a large open grin, drawn as a black-filled D-shape with a white upper-teeth band. Leggings, cuffed moccasins, pouch at the hip.

signature_traits: Oversized, perfectly circular, pure-white head with a bold even near-black outline (head about 1.25x torso width; figure about 3.6 heads tall); no hair, ears, nose or drawn neck
Emoji-minimal face: two small solid-black vertical-oval dot eyes at mid-height and one thin mouth stroke; brows only when emotion needs them
Head turn and tilt shown only by sliding the facial features inside the unchanged circle (shifted for 3/4, single edge eye for profile, low for looking down, blank from behind)
Arms (and legs in motion) are single solid black stick lines with crisp angular elbows and knees, slightly heavier than the head outline
White outlined oval mitten hands with no fingers that overlap or wrap around held objects
Hybrid body: stick head and limbs wearing solid, believable layered clothing (tunic, bib apron, cord belt, pouch, leggings with rolled ankle cuffs, soft rounded shoes) that defines torso and hips

Muted, low-saturation earthy palette (taupe, khaki, olive-brown, warm tan, pale cord cream, weathered grey wood) with no saturated accents; the only whites on the figure are head, hands and neck notch
Costume and props outlined in warm brown-black, slightly wobbly hand-inked contours with ragged, torn, zigzag edges, while head and sticks stay neutral black and vector-clean
Flat local-colour fills with only sparse weathering marks (short double ticks, specks, 1-3 fold strokes, dashed stitches); no cel-shadow shapes, gradients or highlights
Pure white background with no ground line and no cast or contact shadows
Clean model-sheet presentation: title block top-left, 6-view turnaround row, action-pose row, row of 12 head-only expression circles, each with a centred condensed-sans caption, no borders
absent_traits: Hair of any kind, including in the back view
Ears
Nose
Visible neck in front and back views (only a tiny stub in profile)
Skin tone (head and hands are white, not flesh-coloured)
Pupils, eye whites, highlights or eyelashes in normal eyes
Blush, cheeks, chin, jaw or any head shape other than a circle
Fingers, thumbs or nails
Outlined tube limbs, elbows/knees drawn as joints, muscles or anatomy
Eyebrows on calm faces
Gradients, airbrushing, painterly rendering or a 3D/CGI look
Cel-shadow shapes, rim light or specular highlights (except the lighter side of bones)
Cast shadows, contact shadows, ground lines, floor or horizon
Background scenery or colour fields
Panel borders, frames, boxes, dividers or grid lines
Speed lines, motion blur or impact effects
Saturated or bright colours (no red, blue or green accents)
Text, logos or patterns on clothing; speech bubbles; labels inside the artwork
Metal or modern objects (all tools are bone, wood, hide and cord)
adaptation_notes: Locked core for EVERY character prompt on both channels: white circle head with a bold black outline and no hair, ears or nose; dot eyes and a single-stroke mouth from the 12-expression vocabulary; single black stick arms with angular elbows; white oval mitten hands; about 3.6 heads tall with the head about 1.25x torso width; costume and props in flat muted fills with warm brown-black wobbly outlines and sparse tick texture; no shadows, no ground line. Only costume, props, pose and expression change between characters and scenes.

Modern clothing (The Median Worker): replace the hide outfit with simple everyday US clothing built the same way. Use flat, solid garments (T-shirt, button-up, hoodie, work polo, jeans or chinos, sneakers, lanyard, backpack, phone) with warm brown-black outlines, 1-3 fold strokes and a few sparse ticks, and clean rather than torn hems. Keep the same low-saturation, mid-value palette family (greige, faded grey-blue denim, olive, rust-brown, charcoal) so the white head stays the brightest element. Keep trousers drawn as solid leg columns when standing, and state explicitly whether legs become stick lines in motion.

Ancient/prehistoric channel: reuse the reference costume grammar (sleeveless hide tunics, wraps, cloaks, bib aprons, cord belts, pouches, rolled ankle cuffs, soft moccasins, ragged edges). Give each named character one fixed costume signature, a colour within the earthy palette plus one accessory such as a fur cape, bead necklace, headband or carry bag, so characters stay distinguishable without hair or facial detail.

Animals (none in the sheet; inferred): draw them like the props. Use simplified flat-filled silhouettes in muted earthy colours, warm brown-black wobbly outlines, sparse fur ticks or ragged fur edges, and small solid black dot eyes matching the human eyes, with no realistic shading. Keep realistic scale against the 3.6-head humans. Never give animals stick limbs or white circle heads.

Crowds: clone the same base figure and vary only costume colour and cut, one accessory, held prop, height and pose. All heads stay identical white circles with the same outline weight and the same dot-eye, one-line-mouth faces. Background figures may use fewer texture ticks but keep the same line weights. Avoid overlapping heads so each circle stays readable.

Full scenes with backgrounds: leave the character rendering untouched. Draw environments (caves, huts, fire pits, forests, plains, or modern apartments, offices, stores, streets) in the same flat, low-detail way, with warm brown-black outlines and muted fills that are slightly lighter and lower in contrast, so the white heads and black sticks stand out. No photographic texture, painterly gradients or dramatic lighting. The reference has no shadows; if grounding is needed, use at most a small flat neutral ground patch, never cast shadows. Show firelight or night only through flat colour shifts in the background, never by tinting the white head. Prefer a tinted backdrop behind heads so the white circle does not merge into a white sky.

Per-script reference image: reproduce this sheet's structure on pure white at 16:9 (2560x1440). Put our own neutral title block top-left (no third-party name or wording). Row 1 is the turnaround: front, profile facing right, profile facing left, back, 3/4 front, 3/4 back. Row 2 shows every pose the script needs. Row 3 is a strip of head-only expression circles. For several characters, add a front-view lineup on one shared baseline at identical scale, each with a centred name caption. Use condensed sans captions under each item, with no borders, backgrounds or shadows.

Workflow guard: never attach the third-party sheet as an image input and never copy its text. Generate our own sheet from the written spec, then attach OUR sheet as the reference in every later scene generation, and restate the locked core in words each time. Image models tend to drift by adding hair, noses, fingers, skin tone, shading, outlines on limbs and ground shadows.
Keep generated scene images free of text, as the reference keeps text outside the artwork. Captions belong only on the reference sheet; on-screen text and fonts are added later in the video edit.
uncertain: Font identity is a guess: captions look like Roboto Condensed / Helvetica Neue Condensed / Arial Narrow (regular); the title and section headers look like a bold or black condensed grotesque.
Hex values are estimates from a soft, compressed 1644x910 screenshot (plus or minus 5-10 per channel). Costume ink measured #14110C-#18130E and head/stick ink #090909-#0C0C0C.

Stick legs with no leggings appear only in the three dynamic poses (Stretching, Running, Walking); all standing and seated views show leggings. This could be an intentional 'legs become sticks when they bend' rule or an AI-generation inconsistency, so prompts should state one rule explicitly.

The sheet looks AI-generated and has slips that are not style rules: the caption 'Holding up finished / finished clothing' repeats a word, 'Left Side' lacks 'View', and pouch and armhole-patch visibility varies between views.
Profile naming is ambiguous: 'Left Side' shows the figure facing the viewer's right, and 'Right Side View' shows it facing the viewer's left.
It is unclear whether the short arched eyebrows in the 3/4 Front View are part of the default look or incidental; the Front View has none.
Open-mouth convention is inconsistent: the action-pose grin is black-filled with a white teeth band, while the expression-sheet Laughing, Scared, Surprised and Tired mouths have white interiors.
The sheet gives no evidence of how this style shows hair, gender, age, children, skin tone, animals, environments, lighting or shadows in scenes; all such adaptation guidance is inferred.
The black strip about 10 px wide on the left edge and the faint grey line along the bottom edge are assumed to be screenshot or crop artifacts.
The Tired under-eye marks read as one curved line per eye but could be meant as a double line.
The canvas is 1.81:1; the original may have been 16:9 and cropped, so the layout percentages are approximate.
Fine texture marks may have been simplified by downscaling; the original may carry slightly more fur or grain detail.

findings.claim: F1: The Gemini app picks its image model from the chat model. Flash or Pro uses Nano Banana 2. Flash-Lite uses Nano Banana 2 Lite, which is not built for multiple reference images. Nano Banana Pro is only reachable through 'Redo with Pro' on paid plans.
findings.detail: Help center quotes: 'Nano Banana 2 Lite: This option is used when the Gemini model is set to Flash-Lite... It isn't designed for multiple image references or for multiple edits.' 'Nano Banana 2: This option is selected when you make an image request with the Gemini model set to Flash or Pro... It can accept multiple reference images.' 'Nano Banana Pro: Available with a Google AI Plan, this option is available when you have the Gemini model set to Pro and want to redo an image when additional detail is needed.' Steps: generate with Nano Banana 2 or 2 Lite, then 'More > Redo with Pro'. 'If you reach your daily quota of Nano Banana 2 images, you can't redo any additional images with Nano Banana Pro.' Generating and editing images requires age 18+; generating only requires 13+. POSSIBLY OUTDATED: the page does not mention Nano Banana 2.1 yet (see F2/F3).
findings.source_date: unknown (content predates the 2026-10-06 Nano Banana 2.1 rollout)

findings.claim: F2: Nano Banana 2.1 (API id gemini-nano-banana-2.1) launched on 6 October 2026. It is now Google's main image model and is rolling out to the Gemini app, Flow, AI Studio, Search AI Mode, Google Ads and Stitch. Imagen is shut down in the Gemini API.
findings.detail: DeepMind model card: 'Published 6 October 2026'; 'Nano Banana 2.1 is based on Gemini 3.6 Flash'; it lists the Gemini App, Google AI Studio, Gemini API, Google Search AI Mode, Google Ads, Google Flow and Google Stitch as channels. The API doc (last updated 2026-10-09) lists the model ids. Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1) is the 'primary high-efficiency workhorse' with 'improved visual quality, text rendering, multi-turn consistency'. Nano Banana 2 is gemini-3.1-flash-image, now called 'previous-generation'. Nano Banana Pro is gemini-3-pro-image, 'the premium choice for the most complex visual tasks'. Nano Banana 2 Lite is gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image. Nano Banana is gemini-2.5-flash-image ('legacy'). The doc also says: 'Imagen models are shut down. Use Nano Banana models for all image generation tasks.' Google Cloud docs list Nano Banana 2.1 as GA, released Oct 6 2026, with 'Maximum images per prompt: 14'. Google's own X post (x.com/Google/status/2107501211532382687) says it 'starts rolling out today', so individual accounts may get it later.

findings.claim: F3: Plans in the Gemini app: Nano Banana 2 is free. Nano Banana 2.1 needs a Google AI plan (Plus, Pro or Ultra). Paid users can also regenerate an image with Nano Banana Pro via 'Redo with Pro'.
findings.detail: Consumer page quotes: 'Available for free. Upgrade to a Google AI Plan to unlock Nano Banana 2.1, our most advanced image model'. 'Google AI Pro, Plus, Ultra users have access to our best image model, Nano Banana 2.1, and can regenerate images using Nano Banana Pro by selecting the three dot menu and then "Redo with Pro".' 'To access Nano Banana, select "Create images" from the tools menu.' The help center feature table matches: 'Image generation with Nano Banana 2' is available on every plan, and 'Redo images with Nano Banana Pro' only on Plus, Pro and Ultra.
findings.source_date: unknown (mentions Nano Banana 2.1, so on or after 2026-10-06)

findings.claim: F4: Gemini app limits are now based on compute used, with no fixed image count per day. The allowance refreshes every 5 hours up to a weekly cap. Images use more of it than chat. Subscribers who hit the cap are moved to Flash-Lite.
findings.detail: Official quotes: 'Gemini Apps have compute-based usage limits... Your limit refreshes every 5 hours until you reach your weekly limit.' Plan levels: no plan 'Standard limits'; Plus '2x higher than standard limits'; Pro '4x higher than standard limits'; Ultra '5x or 20x higher than AI Pro limits depending on your subscription'. 'Multimedia requests (including images, music, and video) require a lot of thinking power'. 'Some features (like media generation or Deep Research) will consume more of your usage.' 'If you have a Google AI subscription and reach your limit, you can continue your conversation with Flash-Lite.' Long chats with dynamic editing are rated 'Medium' cost, and Google suggests: 'Start a new chat when you move to a new topic.' 9to5Google (2026-05-19) dates the switch from daily caps to compute-based limits to May 2026. Older per-day figures (20/50/100/1,000 Nano Banana 2 images for free/Plus/Pro/Ultra) appear only in older copies of the page and are superseded. The image help page (F1) still mentions a 'daily quota', which is probably stale wording.

findings.claim: F5: Gemini app downloads are 2K with a Google AI plan and only 1K without one. The help center mentions no 4K download in the app.
findings.detail: Quote: 'Download images at at 2K resolution with a Google AI plan or at 1K without an AI plan.' Download path: 'Hover over the image you want to download, and click Download full size'. Conflict: the consumer overview page lists '2K resolution' under the free Nano Banana 2 column. The help center wording is the more specific of the two.

findings.claim: F6: The Gemini app accepts up to 10 files in one prompt, and images count toward that cap. The model behind it can take up to 14 references via the API, but the app's own limit is lower.
findings.detail: Quotes: 'Up to 10 files (subject to availability) can be uploaded in the same prompt.' 'You can add up to 10 (subject to availability) of any kind of supported file in the same prompt, such as documents, images, or videos.' 'All other supported file types can be up to 100 MB.' 'There are rolling limits for how much you can upload and analyze files in a period of time.'

findings.claim: F7: Reference-image limits in the API depend on the model. Nano Banana 2.1 and 3.1 Flash Image take up to 10 object images plus up to 4 character images. Nano Banana Pro takes 6 objects, 5 characters and 3 style references. Nano Banana 2 Lite takes 14 objects and no character references. The total is 14 images.
findings.detail: API doc table under 'Use up to 14 reference images'. Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image: 'Up to 14 images of objects with high-fidelity'; characters N/A. Nano Banana 2.1 and 3.1 Flash Image: 'Up to 10 images of objects with high-fidelity' and 'Up to 4 images of characters to maintain character consistency'. Gemini 3 Pro Image: 'Up to 6 images of objects', 'Up to 5 images of characters', 'Up to 3 images to be used as style references'. The Limitations section adds that 'gemini-2.5-flash-image works best with up to 3 images as input'. Nano Banana 2 Lite is 'Not optimized for multiple reference inputs or multi-turn sequential editing.'

findings.claim: F8: Google's own pages disagree on how many characters stay consistent. Marketing pages say up to 5 characters and 14 objects; the API doc says 4 characters and 10 objects for Nano Banana 2.1 and 3.1 Flash.
findings.detail: Nano Banana 2 launch post (2026-02-26): 'Maintain character resemblance of up to five characters and the fidelity of up to 14 objects in a single workflow'. The DeepMind Nano Banana page, now headed 'Introducing Nano Banana 2.1', still says 'up to five characters – and the fidelity of up to fourteen objects'. Against that, the API doc (2026-10-09) says 'gemini-nano-banana-2.1 and gemini-3.1-flash-image support character resemblance of up to 4 characters and the fidelity of up to 10 objects in a single workflow.' The Nano Banana Pro launch (2025-11-20) says blending 'up to 14 images' with consistency of 'up to 5 people'.

findings.claim: F9: Google's advice on telling references apart: give each attached image an explicit role, give each character a distinct name, and refer to images by order ('first image', 'second image').
findings.detail: Nano Banana Pro tips (2025-11-20): 'Reference inputs: When using uploaded images, clearly define the role of each. (e.g., "Use Image A for the character's pose, Image B for the art style, and Image C for the background environment.")'. DeepMind prompt guide: 'Upload clear reference images, and assign a distinct name to each character or object in your prompt. That way, the model can follow along and maintain their look as you build out your scenes.' API examples use order, e.g. 'Take the blue floral dress from the first image and let the woman from the second image wear it.' Google Cloud's guide (2026-03-06) gives the formula '[Reference images] + [Relationship instruction] + [New scenario]'. The Nano Banana Pro tips post predates Nano Banana 2 and 2.1, but the advice still appears in current pages.

findings.claim: F10: Known Nano Banana 2.1 weaknesses: consistency between input and output is imperfect, it sometimes keeps the pose or layout of an input image, it confuses left and right, and small text renders badly.
findings.detail: Model card limitations: 'Character consistency is not always perfect between input images and generated output image'. 'During image editing, we observe rare instances of persistent subject pose, where structural alignment from the input image is retained in the generated output image'. 'Occasional confusion around spatial localisation (e.g. left/right etc.)'. 'Poor text rendering in small text (often blurry in 1k model), long paragraphs, page length'. 'Still limited in advanced capabilities with world knowledge, 3D reasoning and factuality'. The DeepMind page adds: 'The model excels at character consistency, but it may not always get it right.'

findings.claim: F11: In the API, aspect ratio and size are set with response_format fields aspect_ratio and image_size (1K default, 2K, 4K, written with a capital K). With no ratio set, the output copies the input image's size, or is square when there is no input.
findings.detail: Quotes: 'You can control the aspect ratio and the size of the output image using the aspect_ratio and image_size fields under response_format'. 'By default, the model matches the output image size to that of your input image, or otherwise generates 1:1 squares.' 'Gemini 3 image models generate 1K images by default but can also output 2K, 4K, and 512px' (512px only on 3.1 Flash Image, 'not supported on Gemini Nano Banana 2.1'). 'You must use an uppercase K... Lowercase parameters (e.g., 1k) will be rejected.' Nano Banana 2.1 ratios: 1:1, 1:4, 1:8, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:1, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 8:1, 9:16, 16:9, 21:9.

findings.claim: F12: Nano Banana's '16:9' is slightly wider than true 16:9. The sizes are 1376x768 (1K), 2752x1536 (2K) and 5504x3072 (4K), a 43:24 ratio of about 1.792 against 1.778.
findings.detail: These come from the API doc's size tables for Nano Banana 2.1, 3.1 Flash Image and the Pro table. Derived maths: a 2752x1536 frame scaled to 1440 px high is 2580 px wide, so a 20 px centre crop gives 2560x1440. A 1K frame (1376x768) would need about 1.88x upscaling to reach 1440 px high. Fitting to width instead (2560 px wide gives about 1429 px high) would leave bars.

findings.claim: F13: In the Gemini app, aspect ratio is requested in the prompt text. Google documents no ratio picker in the app; Google's own example prompts write the ratio into the text.
findings.detail: Consumer FAQ: 'Try something like, "Generate an image of a blurry poky porcupine flying in space in the style of an oil painting with 2:3 aspect ratio."' DeepMind guide: 'Prompt for your desired aspect ratio (like 4:3, 1:1, or 9:16) and describe the image format you need – for example, a "widescreen backdrop"... Look for the in-product resolution dropdowns to upscale to 2K or 4K.' Google examples include 'Aspect ratio 16:9.' and 'AR: 16:9' (API doc and Nano Banana 2 post), 'Each image should be a separate output in 16:9 format.' (Nano Banana 2 post), and 'Combine these images into one appropriately arranged cinematic image in 16:9 format' (Nano Banana Pro tips). The Gemini image help page does not mention aspect ratio at all. Third-party reports from 2025, about Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, said prompt-only ratio control in the app was unreliable; those reports may be outdated.
findings.source_date: unknown (plus https://deepmind.google/models/gemini-image/prompt-guide/ undated; 2025 third-party reports e.g. https://en.kocpc.com.tw/?p=13576)

findings.claim: F14: Google Flow makes and edits still images. In the standard prompt box you set aspect ratio, number of outputs and model in the UI, then add reference images ('ingredients'). Edits are non-destructive, with a version history.
findings.detail: Help quotes: 'You can create and edit images directly within your Google Flow projects to use as stand-alone assets or as ingredients for your videos.' Standard prompt box steps: click the model name, click Image, then 'Select your image preferences: Image aspect ratio. Number of outputs you want. The model you want to use.' 'By default, Google Flow sets the model to Nano Banana Pro.' Ingredients are added by dragging media into the prompt box or by 'More > Add to Prompt'. Agent mode can produce many variations, e.g. 'Give me 20 variations of this image with different lighting.' 'When you edit an image in Google Flow, you don't lose the original image' (History panel); you can also crop. The Feb 2026 Flow post adds a lasso tool for natural-language local edits and '@' to reference library assets. The help center does NOT document image download resolution.

findings.claim: F15: Flow offers three image models. Nano Banana Pro is the default for Ultra, Nano Banana 2 Lite is the free default, and Nano Banana 2.1 is the 'standard' model.
findings.detail: Quotes: 'Nano Banana Pro: An advanced image model built for complex designs, highly accurate details, and professional-grade control. It is the default model for Google AI Ultra subscribers.' 'Nano Banana 2 Lite: A highly efficient model for fast, high-quality image generation and editing. It is the default model available at no charge.' 'Nano Banana 2.1: The standard model for fast, high-quality image generation and editing.' This conflicts with F14's 'By default, Google Flow sets the model to Nano Banana Pro'; my guess is that sentence applies to Ultra accounts only. Nano Banana 2 Lite is the model the Gemini app says 'isn't designed for multiple image references' (F1).

findings.claim: F16: Flow 'Characters' are reusable bundles of 1 or 2 reference images (plus an optional voice). A prompt calls them with @Name.
findings.detail: Quotes: 'You can bundle specific visual and audio references into a single, reusable character.' 'Upload or generate 1 or 2 images showing the character's appearance. At least one image is required.' In the image help: 'In the prompt box, type @ followed by your character's name... Describe how your character should be used as a reference.
